user.text:
The `shelfmark` cache in /app sits in front of the catalog API and serves book, author and search requests. Since May 3 its hit rate has dropped and clients see slower answers. The access logs are in /app/logs/access; the service, deploy, configuration, operator and upstream logs are in /app/logs; every revision of the configuration is in /app/config/history (the live file is /app/config/cache.toml); and /app/docs describes the cache. /app/docs/triage.md explains how lost hits are traced and lists the cause classes, and /app/tools/replay.py replays the logged traffic through a copy of the package.

Find every defect in the code shipped in /app/shelfmark that turns requests that should be hits into misses, and write /app/cache-report.json with one entry per defect:

    {"causes": [{"class": "<class>", "file": "<path>", "line": <number>, "requests": <count>, "first": "<request id>"}, ...]}

- `class`: one of the classes in /app/docs/triage.md section 3.
- `file` and `line`: the module, as a path relative to /app (for example `shelfmark/routes.py`), and the number of a line that is wrong, counted in the file as you received it, before your changes.
- `requests`: how many requests in /app/logs/access that were served by the shipped release, logged as `cache=miss`, would have been hits if only this defect had been fixed in the shipped code, with the same traffic, purges, configuration reloads, restarts and flush. A request can count for more than one defect, or for none, for example when it would take two fixes to make it a hit.
- `first`: the id of the earliest of those requests, for example `r0012345`.

Requests served by an earlier release are not counted. Only defects in the shipped code get an entry: traffic, configuration revisions, the upstream, restarts and the flush do not.

Then fix the code under /app/shelfmark so that the cache follows the docs. Do not change anything under /app/tests, /app/tools, /app/docs, /app/logs or /app/config. The package will also be run on other traffic and configurations.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

<path>docs/triage.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Triage
2 	
3 	How a lost hit is traced to its cause.
4 	
5 	## 1. Where to start
6 	
7 	The `stats` lines in `logs/service.log` show the hit rate and the time to
8 	answer hour by hour. The access log shows every request with what the cache
9 	did, so two requests that should share an entry and both missed can be found.
10	A replay (`operations.md` 4) runs the logged traffic through any copy of the
11	package, so the effect of one change to the code on every request can be
12	measured: run the copy and compare with the log.
13	
14	## 2. Things that look wrong and are not
15	
16	- Misses after a restart or a flush, until the entries are stored again.
17	- The first request of a key, and the first request after its entry expired.
18	- The purged book or author itself after a purge.
19	- A slow upstream: misses take longer, but the hit rate does not change.
20	- Requests served by an earlier release did what that release did. Check
21	  `logs/deploy.log`.
22	- A configuration revision that only moves or comments things.
23	
24	## 3. Cause classes
25	
26	| Class | Meaning |
27	|---|---|
28	| `key-params` | A query parameter takes part in the key when the docs leave it out, or the reverse |
29	| `key-normalize` | A parameter value goes into the key without the normalization the docs give, or with another |
30	| `key-vary` | The header-derived part of the key takes more (or fewer) values than the docs allow |
31	| `ttl` | An entry expires earlier or later than its route's configured ttl |
32	| `invalidation` | A purge removes entries it must leave, or leaves entries it must remove |
33	| `capacity` | Entries are dropped before they expire to make room |
34	| `routing` | A request is matched to the wrong route, or a cached route is passed through |
35	| `clock` | Request times are read, ordered or compared wrongly |
</content>

<path>docs/cache.md</path>
<content>
1 	# The cache
2 	
3 	## 1. Cached requests
4 	
5 	| Request | Route | Id |
6 	|---|---|---|
7 	| `GET /books/<id>` | `books` | the book id, digits without a leading zero |
8 	| `GET /authors/<id>` | `authors` | the author id, same form |
9 	| `GET /search` | `search` | none |
10	
11	Any other request (`/health`, other paths, other methods) is passed through
12	and not cached; the access log shows `cache=-` for it. `PURGE` requests
13	(section 4) are answered by the cache itself and also log `cache=-`.
14	
15	## 2. Keys
16	
17	Two requests share an entry exactly when their keys are equal. The key is
18	
19	    <route>|<id>|<parameters>|<locale>
20	
21	2.1 `<parameters>` is built from the query string:
22	
23	- Every query parameter takes part, except parameters whose name is listed in
24	  `ignore_params` (`config.md` 2) and parameters whose name starts with
25	  `utm_`. Names are compared exactly, case included: `UTM_Source` and
26	  `refine` take part.
27	- Values are taken as decoded from the query string (`+` is a space). The
28	  value of `q` is normalized: lowercased, spaces at both ends removed and
29	  every run of whitespace inside replaced by one space, so `Dune  Messiah `
30	  and `dune messiah` are the same search. Other values are kept as they are.
31	- The kept `name=value` pairs are sorted (by name, then value) and joined
32	  with `&`, so the order in which a client sends parameters does not matter.
33	- A request without parameters, or whose parameters are all left out, has an
34	  empty `<parameters>`.
35	
36	2.2 `<locale>` is the locale negotiated from the request's `Accept-Language`
37	header (`locale.md`), spelled exactly as in `locales`, when the route's
38	`vary` list names `Accept-Language`; otherwise it is empty. A route that
39	varies on the locale therefore has at most one entry per supported locale for
40	a given id and parameters.
41	
42	## 3. Expiry
43	
44	A miss stores an entry that expires `ttl` after the time of the request, with
45	the `ttl` of the request's route in the configuration in force at that time
46	(`config.md` 3). A request strictly before the expiry time is a hit; a request
47	at or after it is a miss and stores a new entry. A configuration reload does
48	not change the expiry of entries already stored.
49	
50	## 4. Purge
51	
52	The catalog sends `PURGE /books/<id>` when a book changes and
53	`PURGE /authors/<id>` when an author changes. A purge removes every entry of
54	that one book or author, whatever its parameters and locale, and no other
55	entry: purging book `12` leaves books `120` and `1203` alone. Search entries
56	are never purged; they age out with their `ttl`.
57	
58	## 5. Restart and flush
59	
60	The store is in memory. A restart starts with an empty store, and an operator
61	flush (`operations.md` 3) empties it. The requests after either are misses
62	until the entries are stored again.
63	
64	## 6. Size
65	
66	The store has no entry limit and never evicts an entry before it expires.
67	Expired entries are dropped when a request finds them.
</content>

<path>docs/config.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Configuration
2 	
3 	## 1. Files and revisions
4 	
5 	`config/cache.toml` is the configuration in force. Every revision ever applied
6 	is kept as `config/history/r<rev>.toml` (three digits), and
7 	`logs/config.log` says when each was applied and by whom. Applying a revision
8 	makes the running process reload it (`operations.md` 2); a process that
9 	starts reads the latest applied revision, and its `started` line names it.
10	
11	## 2. Keys
12	
13	| Key | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| `rev` | revision number, a whole number |
16	| `locales` | the locales the catalog has text for, in order of preference for partial matches (`locale.md` 2) |
17	| `default_locale` | the locale of a request that matches none; must be one of `locales` |
18	| `ignore_params` | query parameter names that stay out of the key (`cache.md` 2.1), in any order |
19	| `[routes.<route>]` | one table for each of `books`, `authors` and `search` |
20	| `routes.<route>.ttl` | how long an entry of the route stays fresh (section 3) |
21	| `routes.<route>.vary` | request headers that take part in the key; only `Accept-Language` is supported |
22	
23	Comments, blank lines and the order of tables and keys mean nothing.
24	
25	## 3. Durations
26	
27	A `ttl` is either a whole number of seconds or a string made of a whole
28	number and a unit, without spaces inside:
29	
30	| Written | Duration |
31	|---|---|
32	| `600` | 600 seconds (ten minutes) |
33	| `"750ms"` | 750 milliseconds |
34	| `"90s"` | 90 seconds |
35	| `"10m"` | 10 minutes |
36	| `"6h"` | 6 hours |
37	
38	`600` and `"10m"` are the same ttl. A `ttl` of `0` stores entries that are
39	already expired, which turns caching off for the route. Negative numbers,
40	fractions, other units and booleans are refused when the file is read.
</content>

<path>docs/locale.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Locale negotiation
2 	
3 	The catalog has text in the locales listed in `locales`. A request gets one
4 	of them, chosen from its `Accept-Language` header; the cache key carries the
5 	chosen locale (`cache.md` 2.2), so every request that gets the same locale
6 	shares the entry.
7 	
8 	## 1. Reading the header
9 	
10	The header is a comma separated list of language ranges, each optionally
11	followed by `;q=<weight>`. Ranges are compared without regard to case. A
12	range without a weight has weight 1; a range with weight 0, or with a weight
13	that is not a number, is dropped. The remaining ranges are taken from the
14	highest weight to the lowest, and ranges of equal weight in the order they
15	appear. A missing or empty header has no ranges.
16	
17	## 2. Choosing the locale
18	
19	For each range in that order:
20	
21	1. `*` gives `default_locale`.
22	2. A range equal to a supported locale gives that locale.
23	3. Otherwise, a supported locale whose primary subtag (the part before the
24	   first `-`) equals the range's primary subtag gives that locale; when
25	   several do, the first in `locales` wins.
26	
27	The first range that gives a locale decides. When none does, the request gets
28	`default_locale`. The result is always spelled as in `locales`: with
29	`locales = ["en", "es", "pt-BR"]`, `en-GB` gives `en`, `pt-PT` gives `pt-BR`,
30	`PT-br` gives `pt-BR`, and `it-IT,it;q=0.9` gives `en` when `en` is the
31	default.
32	
33	Examples with `locales = ["en", "en-GB", "fr"]` and `default_locale = "en"`:
34	
35	| Header | Locale |
36	|---|---|
37	| `en-GB,en;q=0.8` | `en-GB` |
38	| `en-AU` | `en` |
39	| `fr-CA;q=0.4, de;q=0.9` | `fr` |
40	| `de, *;q=0.1` | `en` |
41	| `fr;q=0, en-GB;q=0.2` | `en-GB` |
</content>

<path>docs/overview.md</path>
<content>
1 	# shelfmark
2 	
3 	shelfmark is the cache in front of the catalog API. Clients ask it for book
4 	pages, author pages and search results; it answers from its own store when it
5 	holds a fresh entry for the request (a hit) and otherwise asks the catalog
6 	service, stores the answer and returns it (a miss). Misses cost a round trip
7 	to the catalog and its database, so the hit rate sets most of the latency
8 	clients see.
9 	
10	One process serves all traffic, on host `cache-1`. Its store lives in memory:
11	a restart or a flush empties it.
12	
13	## Layout
14	
15	| Path | What it is |
16	|---|---|
17	| `shelfmark/routes.py` | which requests are cached (`cache.md` 1) |
18	| `shelfmark/keys.py` | the cache key of a request (`cache.md` 2) |
19	| `shelfmark/locale.py` | Accept-Language negotiation (`locale.md`) |
20	| `shelfmark/cache.py` | the entry store: expiry, purge, flush (`cache.md` 3 to 5) |
21	| `shelfmark/config.py` | reads a configuration file (`config.md`) |
22	| `shelfmark/service.py` | one request at a time through the above |
23	| `config/cache.toml` | the live configuration; `config/history/` keeps every revision |
24	| `logs/` | access, service, deploy, configuration, operator and upstream logs (`operations.md` 1) |
25	| `tools/replay.py` | replays logged traffic through a copy of the package (`operations.md` 4) |
26	| `tests/` | unit tests: `python3 -m unittest` from this directory |
27	
28	The package only decides hit or miss and what to store. Talking to the catalog
29	and writing the logs is done by the server around it, which is not part of
30	this tree.
</content>

<path>docs/operations.md</path>
<content>
1 	# Operations
2 	
3 	## 1. Logs
4 	
5 	All times are UTC.
6 	
7 	- `logs/access/<date>.log`: one line per request, in the order they were
8 	  served:
9 	
10	  ```
11	  2027-05-03T14:02:11.204Z r0006021 GET /search?q=salt+river&page=1 status=200 cache=miss ms=187 lang="en-GB,en;q=0.8"
12	  ```
13	
14	  The request id, method, target (path and query string as sent), status,
15	  what the cache did (`hit`, `miss` or `-`, `cache.md` 1), the time to
16	  answer in milliseconds and the `Accept-Language` header (`-` when the
17	  request had none).
18	- `logs/service.log`: what the process did besides serving requests:
19	  `started config=r<rev>`, `stopping`, `config reload rev=<rev>`,
20	  `cache flush entries=<n>`, and once an hour a `stats` line for the hour
21	  before it (cached requests, hits, hit rate, the 50th and 95th percentile of
22	  the time to answer, and the entries held).
23	- `logs/deploy.log`: releases, with the time each went live.
24	- `logs/config.log`: configuration revisions, with the time each was applied.
25	- `logs/ops.log`: notes by the operators.
26	- `logs/upstream.log`: the catalog database as its own monitoring sees it,
27	  every five minutes.
28	
29	## 2. Restarts, deploys and reloads
30	
31	The process stops before a deploy or a host change and starts again after
32	it; it serves nothing in between, and it starts with an empty store. A
33	release runs from the first `started` line after its deploy time until the
34	next deploy. A host restart without a deploy (for example a kernel patch)
35	starts the release that was already running. Applying a configuration
36	revision does not restart the process: it logs `config reload` and goes on
37	with the entries it holds.
38	
39	## 3. Flush
40	
41	An operator can empty the store without a restart; `service.log` logs
42	`cache flush` with the number of entries removed, and `ops.log` says why.
43	
44	## 4. Replaying traffic
45	
46	```
47	python3 tools/replay.py [--since TIME] [--until TIME] [--diff] [--pkg DIR] [--root DIR]
48	```
49	
50	reads the service and access logs and the configuration history and runs
51	every request, purge, reload, restart and flush through the package, in log
52	order, starting with an empty store at the last `started` line at or before
53	`--since` (the first `started` line without it). It prints, for each request
54	from `--since` to `--until`, the result in the log and the result of the
55	replay; `--diff` prints only the requests where they differ. Times are
56	written as in the logs, for example `2027-05-03T14:00:05.000Z`. `--pkg`
57	names a directory that holds a `shelfmark` package to use instead of
58	`/app/shelfmark`, for example a copy with one change, and `--root` a
59	directory laid out like `/app` with other logs. Every `started` line runs the
60	same package, so a replay reproduces the log only over the requests the
61	release in `--pkg` actually served.
</content>

1 	# Changelog
2 	
3 	## 2.4.0
4 	
5 	- Search terms are normalized before they go into the key (`cache.md` 2.1).
6 	  2.3.1 kept `q` as sent, so `Dune` and `dune` were stored twice.
7 	- Durations are kept in milliseconds, and a `ttl` can be written with the
8 	  `ms` unit (`config.md` 3).
9 	- Locale negotiation rewritten as one function used by the key builder and
10	  by the response headers (`locale.md`).
11	- The tracking parameter rule moved into the key builder next to
12	  `ignore_params` (`cache.md` 2.1).
13	- Purge removes entries by key prefix instead of walking a per-id index,
14	  which used memory for every stored key.
15	
16	## 2.3.1
17	
18	- `ignore_params` read from the configuration instead of a list in the code.
19	- Authors pages vary on nothing; they have no localized text.
20	
21	## 2.3.0
22	
23	- `PURGE` for authors.
24	- Configuration reloads without a restart.
25	
26	## 2.2.4
27	
28	- Hourly `stats` lines in the service log.
</content>

1 	"""Cache keys (docs/cache.md 2)."""
2 	
3 	from urllib.parse import parse_qsl
4 	
5 	from . import locale
6 	
7 	
8 	def parse_query(query: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
9 	    return parse_qsl(query, keep_blank_values=True)
10	
11	
12	def normalize_q(value: str) -> str:
13	    return " ".join(value.lower().split())
14	
15	
16	def key_params(params, cfg) -> str:
17	    kept = []
18	    for name, value in params:
19	        if name in cfg.ignore_params:
20	            continue
21	        if name == "q":
22	            value = normalize_q(value)
23	        kept.append((name, value))
24	    return "&".join(f"{name}={value}" for name, value in sorted(kept))
25	
26	
27	def build(route: str, ident: str, params, accept_language: str | None, cfg) -> str:
28	    lang = ""
29	    if "Accept-Language" in cfg.routes[route].vary:
30	        lang = locale.negotiate(accept_language, cfg.locales, cfg.default_locale)
31	    return f"{route}|{ident}|{key_params(params, cfg)}|{lang}"
</content>

<path>shelfmark/cache.py</path>
<content>
1 	"""The entry store (docs/cache.md 3 and 4)."""
2 	
3 	
4 	class Cache:
5 	    def __init__(self):
6 	        self.entries: dict[str, int] = {}
7 	
8 	    def get(self, key: str, now_ms: int) -> bool:
9 	        """True when key holds an entry that has not expired at now_ms."""
10	        expires = self.entries.get(key)
11	        if expires is None:
12	            return False
13	        if now_ms < expires:
14	            return True
15	        del self.entries[key]
16	        return False
17	
18	    def put(self, key: str, expires_ms: int) -> None:
19	        self.entries[key] = expires_ms
20	
21	    def purge(self, route: str, ident: str) -> int:
22	        """Removes every entry of one book or author; returns how many."""
23	        prefix = f"{route}|{ident}"
24	        doomed = [k for k in self.entries if k.startswith(prefix)]
25	        for k in doomed:
26	            del self.entries[k]
27	        return len(doomed)
28	
29	    def flush(self) -> int:
30	        count = len(self.entries)
31	        self.entries.clear()
32	        return count
33	
34	    def __len__(self) -> int:
35	        return len(self.entries)
</content>

<content>
1 	"""Reads a cache configuration file (docs/config.md)."""
2 	
3 	import re
4 	import tomllib
5 	from dataclasses import dataclass
6 	from pathlib import Path
7 	
8 	from .errors import ConfigError
9 	from .routes import ROUTES
10	
11	UNITS_MS = {"ms": 1, "s": 1000, "m": 60_000, "h": 3_600_000}
12	DURATION = re.compile(r"([0-9]+)(ms|s|m|h)")
13	VARY = ("Accept-Language",)
14	
15	
16	@dataclass(frozen=True)
17	class Route:
18	    name: str
19	    ttl_ms: int
20	    vary: tuple[str, ...]
21	
22	
23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
24	class Config:
25	    rev: int
26	    locales: tuple[str, ...]
27	    default_locale: str
28	    ignore_params: frozenset[str]
29	    routes: dict[str, Route]
30	
31	
32	def parse_duration_ms(value) -> int:
33	    """The ttl of a route in milliseconds (docs/config.md 3)."""
34	    if isinstance(value, bool):
35	        raise ConfigError(f"not a duration: {value!r}")
36	    if isinstance(value, int):
37	        if value < 0:
38	            raise ConfigError(f"negative duration: {value!r}")
39	        return int(value)
40	    if isinstance(value, str):
41	        m = DURATION.fullmatch(value.strip())
42	        if m:
43	            return int(m.group(1)) * UNITS_MS[m.group(2)]
44	    raise ConfigError(f"not a duration: {value!r}")
45	
46	
47	def parse(text: str) -> Config:
48	    try:
49	        raw = tomllib.loads(text)
50	    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError as e:
51	        raise ConfigError(str(e)) from e
52	    try:
53	        rev = raw["rev"]
54	        locales = tuple(raw["locales"])
55	        default = raw["default_locale"]
56	        ignore = frozenset(raw.get("ignore_params", []))
57	        tables = raw["routes"]
58	    except KeyError as e:
59	        raise ConfigError(f"missing key {e}") from e
60	    if not isinstance(rev, int) or isinstance(rev, bool):
61	        raise ConfigError("rev must be a whole number")
62	    if not locales or default not in locales:
63	        raise ConfigError("default_locale must be one of locales")
64	    routes = {}
65	    for name in ROUTES:
66	        table = tables.get(name)
67	        if table is None:
68	            raise ConfigError(f"no [routes.{name}] table")
69	        vary = tuple(table.get("vary", []))
70	        for header in vary:
71	            if header not in VARY:

4 	def ranges(header: str) -> list[str]:
5 	    """The language ranges of a header, lowercased, best first; q=0 is dropped."""
6 	    found = []
7 	    for pos, part in enumerate(header.split(",")):
8 	        tag, *params = [p.strip() for p in part.split(";")]
9 	        if not tag:
10	            continue
11	        q = 1.0
12	        for p in params:
13	            if p.startswith("q="):
14	                try:
15	                    q = float(p[2:])
16	                except ValueError:
17	                    q = 0.0
18	        if q > 0:
19	            found.append((-q, pos, tag.lower()))
20	    return [tag for _, _, tag in sorted(found)]
21	
22	
23	def primary(tag: str) -> str:
24	    return tag.split("-", 1)[0]
25	
26	
27	def negotiate(header: str | None, supported, default: str) -> str:
28	    """The supported locale a request gets, spelled as in the configuration."""
29	    lowered = [(loc.lower(), loc) for loc in supported]
30	    for rng in ranges(header or ""):
31	        if rng == "*":
32	            return default
33	        for low, loc in lowered:
34	            if low == rng:
35	                return loc
36	        for low, loc in lowered:
37	            if primary(low) == primary(rng):
38	                return rng
39	    return default

20	        """"hit" or "miss" for a cached GET, "-" for anything else."""
21	        path, _, query = target.partition("?")
22	        found = routes.match(path)

31	        if self.cache.get(key, at_ms):

I found four defects in the shipped code, fixed them under `/app/shelfmark`, and wrote `/app/cache-report.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`. The 30 unit tests pass (`python3 -m unittest`, OK). I did not check the fixes against other traffic or configurations. I also did not write an independent model of the docs. So I can't rule out a defect that this traffic never triggers. The classes `routing`, `clock` and `capacity` have no entry, because I found nothing wrong in the code for them.

Shipped 2.4.0 only served requests from the `started` line at 14:00:05 on May 3. Replaying from there reproduces the access log exactly, with 0 differences. The earlier restart at 11:00:05 does not match 2.4.0: the log shows hits that 2.4.0 would miss. That period was served by the earlier release, so I did not count it. This is a departure from the `started`-line rule in `operations.md`, which would put the start of 2.4.0 at 11:00:05. I went by the replay.

| Class | Where | Defect | Requests | First |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key-params` | `shelfmark/keys.py:19` | `utm_*` parameters not on the ignore list (such as `utm_content` and `utm_term`) went into the key. | 764 | `r0009011` |
| `key-vary` | `shelfmark/locale.py:38` | A partial match returned the client's own range (`en-us`) instead of the supported locale (`en`). | 1418 | `r0006627` |
| `invalidation` | `shelfmark/cache.py:23` | The purge prefix had no `|` after the id, so purging book 45 also removed books 450 and 4501. | 16 | `r0007206` |
| `ttl` | `shelfmark/config.py:39` | A ttl written as a whole number (search `600` since r043) was read as 600 ms instead of 600 s. | 274 | `r0011087` |

The fixes:
- **`keys.py`:** skip any parameter whose name starts with `utm_`.
- **`locale.py`:** return the supported locale.
- **`cache.py`:** purge by the prefix `route|id|`.
- **`config.py`:** multiply an integer ttl by 1000.

I got each count by fixing only that defect in a copy of the package. I then ran `tools/replay.py` from 14:00:05 and counted the requests logged as `miss` that the replay turned into hits.

The purge fix also turns one logged hit into a miss (`r0018790`). That request only hit because of the other defects, so it is not part of any count.
